title: Add the ARIA HTML can't give you
prompt:
Four small ARIA jobs on Ticketly's pass card:

1. Mark the **Tickets** link as the current page with `aria-current="page"`.
2. Make **Save to wishlist** a toggle button: start with `aria-pressed="false"` and flip it on each click. Keep the label text unchanged.
3. Make `#basket-status` a **polite** live region so "Ticket added…" is announced.
4. The sticky bar's Add to basket button has `aria-hidden="true"`, which leaves a silent Tab stop. Fix it without removing the button (you may change its text).
hints: aria-current and aria-pressed are plain attributes in the HTML; aria-pressed also needs updating in the click handler.
role="status" is a polite live region. The element already exists at load, which is exactly what live regions need.
Remove aria-hidden from the sticky button. If the duplicate label bothers you, make it more specific, like "Add Friday pass to basket".
explanation: `aria-current="page"` adds "current page" to the Tickets link announcement. The wishlist button keeps its label and exposes its state through `aria-pressed`, which the click handler keeps in sync; the CSS can style from the same attribute. `role="status"` on the existing, empty paragraph means each new message is read politely without moving focus. And the sticky button is visible and focusable again in the accessibility tree: a focusable element must never sit inside `aria-hidden="true"`, because keyboard users reach it while screen readers stay silent.

checks.current-page: Only the Tickets link has aria-current="page"
checks.pressed-toggles: Save to wishlist starts at aria-pressed="false" and toggles on each click
checks.live-region: #basket-status is a live region and announces the basket count
checks.polite: The basket message is polite, not an assertive alert
checks.no-hidden-focusable: No focusable element is hidden with aria-hidden
